name: cloudy-all-mcp
description: Fleet MCP router: list_servers, list_tools(server), call(server, tool, args)

runtime._why_oom_score_adj: #1659: every MCP server on oci-apps is in the last tier the kernel OOM killer picks (_shared/oom-priority.json, tier mcp). Restart policy is 'no' (owner rule), so a killed MCP stays down and its tools are gone until someone starts it by hand. -900 = the host's connectivity tier; not -1000, which would also exempt it from its own cgroup limit.
runtime._why_init: proxy-mcp spawns no children, but tini is cheap insurance against future regressions and unblocks Node SIGTERM handling.

_env_note: env: ROUTER_BEARER (public-route fallback, from the secrets file, never committed); ROUTER_SERVERS optional override.
_dns_doc: The old container keeps these DNS names during the alias release; move them here (dns_aliases) at cutover when the old container is removed.

secrets._doc: One secret by NAME, value only in the private vault at Linux-Containers/infra-api_cloudy-all-mcp/src/secrets.yaml (sops, public fleet recipient; the Ship overlay copies it in and the engine mounts .secrets as env_file). ROUTER_BEARER: 64-hex bearer the router presents to the child MCPs on their public c3-pvt routes (CI sops-create generates it; never printed).

_status: #1450: scaffolded as a standard service (flake, compose, ship engine link); the old cloud-services-mcp keeps serving until this one is healthy.
